items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section VIII, List of Answers on Topics 87:1
items.html: You must know that it is entirely impossible for any advantage to exist in the lower one that is not found in the upper one above it, for whatever exists in the lower one, it must necessarily receive from the upper one above it, since nothing can give what it does not have. Moreover, the essential illumination always remains in the upper one, and only the aspect of a small branch of it reaches the lower one, even though the essential illumination did not come out in the upper one except for the sake of the lower one. And when we say that GAR are the aspect of Hasadim without Hochma, the intention is only with regard to the aspect of desire and will — meaning that the essential desire and yearning of GAR is only to receive and bestow the light of Hasadim, even though the light of Hochma is present in them. Whereas ZAT — their essential matter is toward the illumination of Hochma. (Inner Observation, item 13, Sub Header, “And There Is No”)
